summary: Unexpected fallback window during non-uniform canary traffic split causing mixed-model responses
description:
Issue summary: BrightFin reported intermittent quality regressions in production chat flows during a staged canary rollout. Impact: ~8% of requests for a specific tenant were served by the fallback variant for a short window (~20-45s) despite the tenant being pinned to the new canary variant. Customer observed hallucinations and tokenization mismatches in those responses.

Impact details:
- Customer-facing: sporadic high-severity failures in transactional workflows (payment guidance prompts) causing UX regressions.
- Volume: ~200 requests affected across a 30s window during the rollout spike.
- Business impact: dedicated customer reported slippage against their internal SLO.

Environment: production cluster in us-east; dedicated pool for BrightFin; canary configured as 15% traffic weight with traffic mirroring enabled for prewarm.

Observed behavior: routing logs show cohort-level pin eviction and routing decisions to fallback variant coincident with elevated health-probe latencies from the edge prewarm path. Expected behavior: tenant pins should persist for the session and not fall back unless explicit health failures on serving instances are detected.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Create a tenant-scoped canary by promoting a new model variant and apply non-uniform traffic split (15% canary, 85% stable) with traffic mirroring/prewarm enabled.
2) Simulate a short latency spike on the edge prewarm health probe (200-500ms delays).
3) Send steady request stream for the pinned tenant and observe routing logs and model fingerprints returned.
4) Verify whether session pin lease renewals are missed and whether routing shifts to fallback variant for short window.

Notes: reproduction requires non-uniform weight distribution and traffic mirror prewarming. The issue did not appear in a uniform 50/50 split in our quick tests.
steps_to_reproduce: Promote a new model variant for a tenant and configure canary with 15% traffic weight and traffic mirroring enabled.
Begin a steady request stream from the tenant (10r/s) pinned to the canary cohort.
Inject additional latency (200-500ms) into the edge prewarm health probe path for ~30s.
Inspect routing decision logs and model fingerprints returned to the client for signs of fallback responses.

investigation_notes: 03-10 09:30 - Support (Aisha): Customer provided sample request IDs and timestamps; observed mixed model fingerprints in response bodies.
03-10 10:10 - SRE (Marco): Retrieved routing logs and identified lease_renewal misses coincident with elevated prewarm probe latencies on the edge path.

03-10 11:02 - Eng (R. Flores): Hypothesis: non-uniform traffic snapshot merging created transient snapshot mismatch between edge prewarm and control-plane, causing session-lease renewal logic to treat the tenant as unpinned for a short window.

03-10 11:40 - Eng: Found that lease-renewal uses snapshot-version comparisons and a race exists when mirror/prewarm introduces an additional snapshot ahead of commit; when weight vectors differ, the renewal path fails and lease falls back to default TTL behavior (15s), allowing a fallback decision before renewal completes.
03-11 08:22 - Eng: Confirmed by replaying traffic in a staging cluster and reproducing a 25-40s fallback window when probe latency was injected and canary weight was <20%.
03-11 14:00 - Mitigation applied: temporarily increased session-lease TTL for BrightFin to 60s and applied a tenant-scoped override to force pin retention during the rollout window.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Aisha (Support): Thanks BrightFin for the samples. Noting that affected requests are primarily within 09:14-09:15 UTC window. Escalating to SRE/Eng.
2026-03-10 10:25 - Marco (SRE): Retrieved edge and control-plane logs; attaching trace ids 7a9c3f/8b2d77. Initial hypothesis: lease renewal race during non-uniform snapshot merge. Eng engaged.

2026-03-11 11:05 - Raul Flores (Engineering): Created fix proposal in PR #4128 to make lease-renewal resilient to snapshot skew by matching on cohort-majority fingerprint instead of strict snapshot equality. Repro test added to ci/staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4128

2026-03-12 08:30 - Marco (SRE): Applied tenant-scoped TTL increase and forced pin retention as an emergency mitigation. Monitoring shows no further fallback windows for BrightFin since 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 09:05 - BrightFin (Customer): Confirming quality improved; no further mixed-model outputs observed in our production traffic. Awaiting permanent fix.
2026-03-12 12:40 - Aisha (Support): Marking as In Progress. Eng to track the PR through staging -> canary -> prod; will schedule a postmortem if fix spans >72 hours.
resolution: Mitigation applied: tenant-scoped TTL increased to 60s and temporary pin-retention override implemented. Permanent fix proposed (PR #4128) to change lease-renewal snapshot comparison logic to be tolerant of non-uniform snapshot merges. Plan: backport to stable branch, run canary, then roll to prod. Postmortem pending after full fix rollout.
